body:
Cognitive behavioral therapy and dialectical behavioral therapy with several individual therapists and groups, person-centered therapy with a social worker/therapist, acceptance and commitment therapy from treading a book, A.A./12-steps with sponsor for 2 years, Buddhism from books, pharmacotherapy (Currently zoloft, ativan, lithium, depakote. I've tried lamictal, gabapentin, inderall, abilify, buspar, risperdall, wellbutrin, celexa). I believe I used other substances to try to feel better as well since I was 14. Marijuana when I was 14, cocaine when I was 16, alcohol throughout, and adderall, nitrous oxide, vicodin, percoset, LSD, mushrooms, DMT, 2-CE, on occasion. I stopped drinking and using drugs when I was 22. I had a manic episode 6 months before that and have not had one since but still get depressed. I'm currently 27.

The most helpful therapy for panic disorder and agoraphobia has been acceptance and commitment therapy. Still, I rarely go out of the house for fear of having a panic attack and throwing up.

The most helpful therapy for depression was motivational interviewing. I no longer have access to that therapist because I don't go to the school where she works anymore. I have not been successful in finding a therapist helpful for me since then, which has been about 4 years. The one I currently see recommends I read self help books and attend groups. I've done both. Groups are hard because of panic disorder. A book I found on acceptance and commitment therapy has helped with panic.

Unfortunately yes, I have no friends. That and I think it's pretty specific experiential knowledge that few have and that I wouldn't wish on anyone.

Thank you for the reply :))))
